# Part F: Industrial cloud architecture on Microsoft Azure

**Chosen platform:** Microsoft Azure, Central India (Pune), paired with South India (Chennai). The reasoning is in [Part C](part_c_decision.md).

**Diagrams.** All are generated by `python python/make_diagrams.py`; each has a PNG, an SVG and a `.dot` source in `diagrams/`.

| `02_reference_architecture` | Detailed architecture with official Azure icons |
| `03_security_zones` | Purdue levels and IEC 62443 zones and conduits |
| `04_er_diagram` | Database ER diagram, generated from the live PostgreSQL catalog |
| `05_data_pipeline` | Datasets → scripts → outputs |

## F.1 Block-to-service mapping

| # | Block | Azure service / component | Role in this factory | Evidence / status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **CNC / PLC / Sensors** | Fanuc 0i-MF / 31i-B5 and SINUMERIK 828D / 840D sl controllers; one tri-axial spindle accelerometer per machine (2 kHz) | 10 slow streams (spindle temperature, coolant temperature, spindle vibration RMS, RPM, spindle current, feed-axis load, hydraulic pressure, coolant flow, power, door/cycle status) plus 1 fast vibration channel | Controller OPC UA needs FASOPC or the SINUMERIK OPC UA option [S79][S80] |
| 2 | **OPC UA / MQTT** | OPC UA (port 4840, Sign & Encrypt) machine → gateway; MQTT 3.1.1/5 over TLS gateway → cloud | Unified Namespace topics: `tier1/<site>/<area>/<machine>/<stream>` (e.g. `tier1/chakan/powertrain/hmc-07/vibration/features`) | Event Grid MQTT broker GA with MQTT v5 [S39] |
| 3 | **Edge Gateway** | **Azure IoT Operations** on **Arc-enabled K3s / AKS Edge Essentials**, two industrial PCs per plant (HA). OPC UA connector, MQTT broker, data flows. A durable outbox sized for 7 days. | Protocol conversion; 1-s vibration features (143× reduction); per-second batching; local alarms; store-and-forward | AIO GA 1.2–1.4 [S32]; OPC UA connector [S33]; AIO offline ≤ 72 h, so a durable outbox is added [S34][S35] |
| 4 | **Cloud Data Ingestion** | **Azure IoT Hub (S2 ×2)**: per-gateway X.509 identity, routing. **Event Hubs** for fan-out; **Fabric Eventstreams** as the stream-processing front end | 259.2 M batched messages per month (8.64 M/day) | IoT Hub tiers [S46]; Central India pricing [S47]; Eventstreams MQTT source [S40] |
| 5 | **Data Lake / Time-Series Storage** | **ADLS Gen2** (bronze raw JSON → silver Parquet → gold aggregates); **Fabric Eventhouse / Azure Data Explorer** for the hot 30–90 days with KQL time-series functions | 12-month lake retention ≈ 0.4 TB compressed (6.9× Parquet+Zstd measured) | ADLS pricing [S49]; ADX time-series [S42]; Time Series Insights retired, replaced by ADX [S28] |
| 6 | **SQL Database** | **Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server**, with the schema in `sql/01_schema.sql` unchanged (raw / core / analytics; TimescaleDB path documented) | Hourly machine KPIs, master data, alarms, OEE / MTBF views for apps and reports | Flexible Server pricing in Central India [S50] |
| 7 | **Python Analytics / AI** | **Azure Machine Learning** (training, registry, batch scoring) and Fabric notebooks; models deployed to the edge as containers through IoT Operations | Isolation Forest vibration anomaly (ROC-AUC 0.98), 24-h failure risk, failure-mode classifier | Eventhouse anomaly functions [S40][S42] |
| 8 | **Dashboard** | **Power BI** and **Fabric Real-Time Dashboards** for management; this project's **Streamlit** app (App Service or Streamlit Community Cloud) | OEE, quality, alarms, machine health, PdM risk | Power BI native in Fabric [S40] |
| 9 | **Manufacturing Decision** | **Fabric Activator** → Teams / e-mail alerts; maintenance work orders in the CMMS / SAP PM | Wear-based tool change (reject rate 1.50% → 0.92%, indicative); risk-ranked maintenance | Activator in Fabric RTI [S40] |
| – | **Security & operations** | Entra ID + managed identities, Key Vault (certificates), **Defender for IoT** OT sensor in *locally managed* mode, Sentinel, Azure Monitor | OT network visibility, secrets, audit | AIO PKI and X.509 [S34]; Defender for IoT cloud mode routes to East US, so local mode is used [S55] |

**Edge hardware per plant (one-time cost, `cost_model.md`):**
- 2 × fanless industrial PCs (8 cores, 32 GB RAM, 1 TB SSD) running K3s, in a high-availability pair;
- an industrial firewall at the Level 3.5 DMZ;
- a SPAN port for the Defender for IoT sensor.

## F.2 Why this shape

- **Thin cloud ingress, rich edge.**
  - Part A measured 19.2 Mbps of raw vibration for the fleet against 0.13 Mbps of features. Only features and 1 Hz data cross the WAN: about 0.69 Mbps for the whole fleet, under 1% of a typical 100 Mbps plant link.
  - The naive one-message-per-reading design would cost ₹14–30 lakh/month in ingestion (`cost_model.md`).
- **Two time-series tiers.**
  - Eventhouse/ADX for fast recent queries (the dashboard's "last 30 days").
  - ADLS Parquet for cheap long history and model training.
  - PostgreSQL holds only hourly KPIs and master data: 185 B/row measured, so 876,100 rows take 162 MB.
- **Region choice.**
  - Central India is in Pune, beside the Chakan plant, and is paired with South India in Chennai, beside Oragadam [S43].
  - IoT Hub keeps data in the geography [S45].
  - The two residency caveats and their mitigations are in [Part C §C.4](part_c_decision.md).

## F.3 Security zoning (Purdue / IEC 62443), diagram `03_security_zones`

| Zone (Purdue level) | Contents | Target security level (SL-T) | Conduit out |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cell / machine zone (L0–L2), one VLAN per shop floor | CNC controllers, PLCs, safety I/O, accelerometers, HMIs | SL 2–3 | **C1**: OPC UA 4840 Sign & Encrypt to the gateway only |
| Site operations zone (L3) | Edge gateway cluster, plant historian / Grafana, Defender for IoT sensor (passive SPAN) | SL 3 | **C2**: MQTT/TLS 8883, outbound only |
| Industrial DMZ (L3.5) | MQTT relay, patch server, jump host for vendor access (MFA, session recording) | SL 3 | **C3**: TLS 1.2+ to Azure via VPN / private peering |
| Enterprise IT (L4) | ERP/SAP, MES reports, office users | SL 2 | **C4**: HTTPS with Entra ID |
| Cloud (L5) | IoT Hub, ADX, ADLS, PostgreSQL (private endpoints), Azure ML, Power BI | SL 2 | – |

**Rules:**
- All flows are initiated from the lower level to the higher one. There is no inbound path from the internet or Level 4 to Levels 0–2.
- Firewalls deny by default at every conduit.
- Machine protection and alarms never depend on the cloud.
- Every gateway has its own X.509 certificate, kept in Key Vault and rotated.
- Vendor remote access only goes through the time-boxed, audited jump host (conduit C5).

## F.4 Working demonstration in this repository

| Architecture block | Implemented here | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Edge feature extraction | `python/edge/bosch_features.py` on all 1,702 real Bosch files | 143× reduction per machine-second; 120× measured on the full dataset (`docs/results/edge_reduction.json`) |
| Edge gateway + MQTT + store-and-forward | `python/edge/edge_gateway.py`, `mqtt_broker.py`, `cloud_subscriber.py` | 482 produced / 482 stored / 0 lost / 0 duplicates across a subscriber outage and a 12-s WAN outage (`docs/results/mqtt_demo_summary.json`, figure `edge_mqtt_store_and_forward.png`) |
| SQL database | PostgreSQL 16 with `sql/01_schema.sql` | 876,100 fact rows loaded at about 47k rows/s with COPY; 8 required + 10 advanced queries (`sql/results/`) |
| Analytics / AI | `python/ml/` | Model results in `docs/results/ml_*.json` |
| Dashboard | `dashboard/` (Streamlit, 8 pages) | Local mode reads PostgreSQL; hosted mode reads Parquet |
